cells.tense: You are standing at the clearing, and the ground under you is solid.
cells.ask: Name one distinction you have been holding privately, and say it out loud to somebody today, once.
cells.core: You can tell what matters from what only looks like it does, and you do it quietly, in your own head. The false thing has already fallen away. Not because someone shook it loose — because you finally saw through it. When that happens it isn't damage. The old structure lets go because it couldn't hold what you now see. You don't need more proof that it was false. You have it. The certainty isn't loud. It sits there and you can stand on it. What keeps this steady is small: make one distinction at a time, let it settle, then look at the next. No rush in it. Just attention, offered without force. The clearing isn't the end of the work. It's the floor under it, and the work is quiet, and it can hold you.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a collapse that has not happened, and the bracing has weight.
cells.ask: Take one thing you keep re-checking, leave it alone for the rest of the day, then note what actually happened.
cells.core: You are separating things ahead of time. Every flaw gets spotted before it surfaces, every structure gets tested against a future that hasn't arrived, and careful attention has turned into pressure. It feels like staying ahead. From outside it looks like guarding against a collapse that isn't here yet — and you are the only one living in that room. Some collapses don't need your hand. They aren't failures coming for you. They are false structures letting go when they are done, and the release comes from completion, not defeat. Let one check drop. Not forever. For today. The work still stands without the bracing holding it up. The waiting isn't the work. The watching isn't the work. The refining can happen without fear running behind it.

cells.tense: You shut the door on the clearing a while back, and you are still at it.
cells.ask: Tell one person one distinction you have kept to yourself, and let what they say back count for something.
cells.core: The sharpness is still in you, but it has gone quiet instead of working. You know how to tell one thing from another. You are just not doing it in front of anyone, or even for yourself. When you pick something up, it dissolves under your attention and nothing holds long enough to be useful. What stops this isn't more thinking. It's the exchange — the give and take that would let the distinction land somewhere other than inside your own head. Say the thing you have been keeping, and let the other person's reaction matter. What comes back won't be a verdict. It will be contact, and contact is what pulls the current back through. One conversation is enough to start.

cells.tense: You are already sorting what matters from what doesn't, and calling it obvious.
cells.ask: Pick one judgment you have been treating as obvious and say it plainly: you made that call.
cells.core: You are already making the call. In the middle of a conversation, in the quiet before a decision, in what you repeat and what you let fall — you distinguish, all day long, and the distinctions hold. What's off isn't the doing. It's that you describe it as if it were happening to you. The situation sorted itself out. The obvious answer was obvious. The false thing fell on its own. The deciding keeps running, and you haven't owned it. When you stop noticing that you are the one deciding, the practice keeps going but stops feeding anything. The correction is smaller than it sounds. No announcement, no defense. Just recognize, once, the thing you chose, and let it be yours.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that in the Balanced cell, the practice itself is already public — the record calls it private, 'distinctions nobody else can see yet.' The reader could reasonably say the cell is describing completion when the capacity is still solitary. The ask survives being wrong: it works whatever the person's draw, because it only asks for the one distinction they already hold. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any close that tells them where they belong; 'that is how the ground gets made' was cut for that reason.
